source_text:
ἀπαγαγεῖν αὐτὸν ἄκριτον, ἀναπολόγητον. Καὶ γὰρ ἦν τὸ ἔγκλημα θεοσέβεια,
ἔγκλημα ὃ λαμπρᾷ τῇ φωνῇ ὁ δράσας καθωμολόγει· καὶ μηδενὸς μὲν ἐρωτῶντος
τοῖς ἔργοις ἐδείκνυε, πυνθανο μένου δὲ περιχαρῶς ἐβόα. Ἐλθόντες οὖν οἱ τῆς
1
ἐκείνου τιμωρίας δήμιοι καὶ τῆς ἡμετέρας ἑορτῆς αἴτιοι παρ' αὐτῷ τῷ ζητουμένῳ
κατέλυσαν, οὔτε γινώσκοντες οὔτε μὴν γινωσκόμενοι. Ἐν ἀπορρήτῳ δὲ τέως εἶχον
τῆς ἐπιδημίας τὴν πρόφασιν, ἵνα πρότερον ἐκδιδαχθέντες παρὰ τῶν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως,
τίς ὁ Φωκᾶς καὶ 9.120 ὅπου διάγει, ἀθρόον ἐπιστάντες συλλάβωσιν, ὡς Ἰουδαῖοι ποτε
ἐν τῷ κήπῳ μετὰ Ἰούδα τὸν Κύριον. Ἐλελήθεσαν δὲ εἴσω δικτύων τὴν θήραν
ἔχοντες, οἱ κύνες τὸν ἀρνειόν, οἱ λύκοι τὸν ἀμνόν, καὶ συνανεπαύετο ταῖς
παρδάλεσιν ὁ ἔριφος καὶ τοῖς λύκοις ὁ ἀρνὸς συνεβόσκετο καὶ οἱ λέοντες ἅμα τῷ
μόσχῳ κοινὴν ἐποιοῦντο τὴν δίαιταν. Ἐπεὶ δέ, οἷα φιλεῖ γίνεσθαι, τράπεζα καὶ
συνήθεια τὸ θαρρεῖν ἀλλήλοις παρέσχον, διεπυνθάνετο παρ' αὐτῶν ὁ μάρτυς τίνες
τε εἶεν καὶ τίνος χάριν τὴν αὐτοῦ πόλιν κατέ λαβον. Οἱ δὲ τὴν πρόθυμον δεξίωσιν
καὶ φιλοξενίαν τοῦ ἀνδρὸς αἰδεσθέντες μηδενί τε τὸ λεχθησόμενον ἐξειπεῖν
παραγγείλαντες, γνωρίζουσιν αὐτῷ τὸ ἀπόρρητον καὶ τὸ τῆς ἐπιβουλῆς
ἐξαγορεύουσι δρᾶμα, καὶ ὅτι Φωκᾶν ἐπὶ τιμωρίᾳ ζητοῦσι λαβεῖν· ὅθεν πρὸς τῇ
φιλοξενίᾳ καὶ ταύτην ἠξίουν χαρίσασθαι τὴν εὐεργεσίαν, καὶ συγκαμεῖν αὐτοῖς εἰς
τὴν θήραν τοῦ ζητουμένου. Ἤκουσεν ὁ τοῦ Κυρίου θεράπων καὶ ἀτρέπτῳ τῇ ψυχῇ
τὸν λόγον δεξάμενος, οὐ ταπεινόν τι καὶ ἀγεννὲς ἔπαθεν ἢ ἐφθέγξατο· οὐδὲ τὸν
κίνδυνον ἀποδειλιάσας πρὸς φυγὴν ἔβλεψε, καὶ ταῦτα πολλὴν ἔχων πρὸς τοῦτο τὴν
ἐξουσίαν, ὅτι μηδὲ δῆλος ἦν ἔτι αὐτὸς ὢν ὁ παρ' ἐκείνων ἐπιζητούμενος· ἀλλὰ πᾶν
τοὐναντίον ἐποίει, ἀνδρίζεσθαι μᾶλλον καὶ οὐχὶ φεύγειν προῃρημένος. Ἀμέλει καὶ
πρὸς τὴν ἀξίωσιν αὐτῶν ἐπινεύει· Κἀγώ, φησίν, ὑμῖν εἰς τὸ προκείμενον
συνεφάψομαι. Γινώσκω γὰρ τὸν ἄνδρα καὶ ῥᾳδίως ἀναζητήσας εὑρήσω· οὐκ εἰς
μακρὰν δὲ τοῦτον, ἀλλ' εἰς τὴν ἐπιοῦσαν καὶ αὐτοῖς ὑμῖν ἐπιδείξω· μόνον ὑμεῖς ἐπὶ
τῆς πενιχρᾶς μου ταύτης καταγωγῆς ἀναπαύσασθε. Οὕτω βεβαίαν αὐτοῖς
ἐγγυησάμενος τὴν ὑπόσχεσιν πράγμασιν ἑαυτὸν καταμερίζει δυσί, τῇ τε δεξιώσει
τῶν ἑαυτοῦ φονέων καὶ τῇ ἑτοιμασίᾳ τοῦ τάφου. Εὐτρεπίσας δὲ τό τε ὄρυγμα καὶ τὰ
περὶ ταφὴν ἀναγκαῖα, προσελθὼν αὐτοῖς τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ, Ἐπιμελῶς ὑμῖν, ἔφη, τὸν
Φωκᾶν ἀνεζήτησα καὶ ἕτοιμον ἤδη τὸ θήραμα· καί, εἰ δοκεῖ, συλληφθήτω. Τῶν δὲ
εἰπόντων ἐκ περιχαρείας· Καὶ ποῦ ὁ ἀνήρ; Οὐ πόρρω, φησίν, ἀλλὰ μεθ' ὑμῶν· αὐτὸς
δὲ ὑμῖν οὗτος ἐγώ· καὶ χρήσασθε τῷ πράγματι καὶ πληρώσατε τὸν τῆς ὁδοιπορίας καὶ
τοῦ πόνου σκοπόν.
thought_title: Phocas reveals himself to the soldiers
orientation: Asterius is recounting how soldiers sent to arrest Phocas lodged with him without recognizing him, and now he tells how Phocas revealed his identity.
pass_a_gloss: to lead him away unjudged, without defense. For the charge was reverence for God, a charge which the one who did it confessed with a loud voice; and when no one asked, he showed it by his deeds, but when someone inquired, he shouted it out with joy. So the executioners of that man's punishment and the causes of our feast came and lodged with the very man being sought, neither knowing nor indeed being known. And for the time being they kept the pretext of their visit in secret, so that first having learned from those outside the city who Phocas is and where he stays, they might suddenly stand upon him and seize him, as the Jews once in the garden with Judas seized the Lord. But they had escaped notice, holding their prey inside their nets, the dogs the ram, the wolves the lamb, and the kid was resting with the leopards and the lamb was grazing with the wolves and the lions together with the calf made their dwelling common. But when, as is wont to happen, table and familiarity gave them confidence in one another, the martyr inquired of them who they were and for what reason they had come to his city. And they, respecting the eager welcome and hospitality of the man and having instructed him to tell no one what would be said, make known to him the secret and confess the drama of the plot, and that they seek to take Phocas for punishment; wherefore in addition to the hospitality they also asked him to grant this benefaction, and to labor with them in the hunt for the one being sought. The servant of the Lord heard and, receiving the word with an untroubled soul, suffered or uttered nothing lowly and ignoble; nor did he, fearing the danger, look to flight, and this though he had much freedom for this, because he was not even yet revealed as being the one sought by them; but he did the exact opposite, having chosen rather to be courageous and not to flee. Indeed he also nods to their request: I too, he says, will join with you in the matter set before us. For I know the man and having searched easily I will find him; and not after a long time, but on the coming day I will show him to you yourselves; only you rest in this poor lodging of mine. Having thus guaranteed to them a firm promise, he divides himself between two tasks, the welcoming of his own murderers and the preparation of the tomb. And having prepared the pit and the things necessary for burial, he came to them on the next day and said, I have carefully searched for Phocas for you, and the prey is already ready; and, if it seems good, let him be seized. And when they said with great joy, And where is the man? Not far, he says, but with you; this very one before you is I myself; and use the matter and fulfill the purpose of your journey and toil.

choices.english: to lead him away unjudged, without defense
choices.why: Keeps the two adjectives as parallel predicates describing the manner of arrest, preserving the legal language of condemnation without trial.
rejected: to lead him away without trial or defense

choices.term: Ἐλελήθεσαν δὲ εἴσω δικτύων τὴν θήραν ἔχοντες
choices.english: But they had escaped notice, holding their prey inside their nets
choices.why: The subject is the soldiers; the perfect tense indicates their state of unawareness—they held the prey (Phocas) within their nets without realizing it.
rejected: they had escaped notice, holding their prey inside their nets

choices.term: οἱ κύνες τὸν ἀρνειόν, οἱ λύκοι τὸν ἀμνόν
choices.english: the dogs the ram, the wolves the lamb
choices.why: Preserves the ironic reversal: the predators (dogs, wolves) are the soldiers, and the prey (ram, lamb) is Phocas, but they are at peace together.
rejected: the dogs had the ram, the wolves had the lamb

choices.why: Renders the compound verb's sense of shared toil in the hunt, emphasizing the soldiers' request for Phocas's help.
Conveys the steadfastness and calm of Phocas's inner disposition, matching the adjective's sense of not being turned or shaken.
Uses the glossary term for καταγώγιον, here in its related noun form, to keep the hospitality theme consistent.

bible_refs.note: ὡς Ἰουδαῖοι ποτε ἐν τῷ κήπῳ μετὰ Ἰούδα τὸν Κύριον

pass_b_english: They were to lead him away unjudged, without defense. For the charge was reverence for God, a charge the one who committed it confessed with a clear voice; and when no one asked, he showed it by his deeds, but when someone inquired, he shouted it out with joy. So the executioners of his punishment—and the cause of our festival—came and lodged with the very man they were seeking, neither knowing him nor being known by him. For the time being they kept the reason for their visit secret, so that they might first learn from those outside the city who Phocas was and where he stayed, and then suddenly surround and seize him, as the Jews once did with Judas in the garden when they seized the Lord (cf. John 18:3). But they were unaware, holding the prey inside their nets: the dogs with the ram, the wolves with the lamb, and the kid rested with the leopards, and the lamb grazed with the wolves, and the lions shared their common life with the calf. And when, as usually happens, table and familiarity gave them confidence in one another, the martyr asked them who they were and for what reason they had come to his city. They, out of respect for the man's eager welcome and hospitality, and after instructing him to tell no one what would be said, made known to him the secret and disclosed the plot of their scheme—that they were seeking Phocas to take him for punishment. Therefore, in addition to his hospitality, they asked him to grant them this favor as well: to labor with them in the hunt for the man they sought. The servant of the Lord heard this and received the word with an untroubled soul. He suffered nothing low or ignoble, nor did he say anything of the sort; nor did he shrink from the danger and look to flight, even though he had great freedom to do so, since it was not yet clear that he himself was the one they were seeking. But he did exactly the opposite, choosing rather to act with courage and not to flee. And indeed he nodded to their request. "I too," he says, "will join you in the task before us. For I know the man and will easily search him out and find him. I will show him to you not after a long time, but on the next day. Only rest here in my poor lodging." Having thus given them a firm promise, he divided himself between two tasks: welcoming his own murderers and preparing his tomb. When he had made ready the grave and the things necessary for burial, he came to them on the next day and said, "I have searched diligently for Phocas for you, and the prey is now ready. And if it seems good, let him be seized." When they said with joy, "And where is the man?" he said, "Not far off, but with you. I myself am he. Do what you will with the matter and fulfill the purpose of your journey and labor."

problems.quote: the dogs were the ram, the wolves were the lamb
problems.source_quote: οἱ κύνες τὸν ἀρνειόν, οἱ λύκοι τὸν ἀμνόν
problems.why: Missing verbs; should be 'the dogs [were with] the ram, the wolves [with] the lamb' or similar.
problems.fix: the dogs with the ram, the wolves with the lamb

problems.source_quote: ὡς Ἰουδαῖοι ποτε ἐν τῷ κήπῳ μετὰ Ἰούδα τὸν Κύριον
problems.why: The allusion is to Jesus' arrest in Gethsemane, but John 18:2-3 mentions Judas knowing the place, not 'with Judas' as companion to the Jews. The parallel is closer to the Synoptics or John 18:3 generally, but 'with Judas' is odd for John.

problems.quote: But the prey had escaped their notice while they held it inside their nets
problems.source_quote: Ἐλελήθεσαν δὲ εἴσω δικτύων τὴν θήραν ἔχοντες
problems.why: Subject is 'they' (the hunters), not 'the prey'; they held the prey in their nets unknowingly.
problems.fix: But they were unaware, holding the prey inside their nets
problems.ruling: Ἐλελήθεσαν is plural 'they were ignorant'; English wrongly makes 'the prey' subject, misleading reader about who was unaware.

problems.quote: and the kid rested with the leopards, and the lamb grazed with the wolves, and the lions shared their common life with the calf
problems.source_quote: καὶ συνανεπαύετο ταῖς παρδάλεσιν ὁ ἔριφος καὶ τοῖς λύκοις ὁ ἀρνὸς συνεβόσκετο καὶ οἱ λέοντες ἅμα τῷ μόσχῳ κοινὴν ἐποιοῦντο τὴν δίαιταν
problems.why: Misidentifies animals: ἀρνειόν/ἀμνόν are both 'lamb/ram,' not 'kid'; ἔριφος is 'kid.' First clause has 'the kid rested with leopards,' second 'the lamb grazed with wolves'—but source has lamb with leopards, kid with wolves.
problems.fix: and the lamb rested with the leopards, and the kid grazed with the wolves, and the lions shared their common life with the calf
problems.ruling: ἔριφος=kid, ἀρνειόν/ἀμνόν=lamb; English swaps animals: source has kid with leopards, lamb with wolves, reversed.

edits.new: the dogs with the ram, the wolves with the lamb

edits.new: But they were unaware, holding the prey inside their nets

edits.old: and the kid rested with the leopards, and the lamb grazed with the wolves

fixed: Corrected 'the dogs were the ram, the wolves were the lamb' to 'the dogs with the ram, the wolves with the lamb' to reflect the source's missing verbs and the intended contrast.
Changed '(John 18:2-3)' to '(cf. John 18:3)' because the source's 'with Judas' does not match John 18:2-3, where Judas is not a companion of the Jews.

Corrected 'But the prey had escaped their notice while they held it inside their nets' to 'But they were unaware, holding the prey inside their nets' because the source's subject is the hunters, not the prey.
Corrected the animal identifications: 'the lamb rested with the leopards, and the kid grazed with the wolves' to match the source's ἀρνειόν/ἀμνόν as lamb and ἔριφος as kid.

problems.why: Subjects are swapped: the kid rested with leopards, the lamb grazed with wolves. English reverses which animal does which action.

problems.fix: the kid rested with the leopards, and the lamb grazed with the wolves

last_rejected.quote: as the Jews once did with Judas in the garden when they seized the Lord (cf. John 18:3)
last_rejected.source_quote: ὡς Ἰουδαῖοι ποτε ἐν τῷ κήπῳ μετὰ Ἰούδα τὸν Κύριον
last_rejected.why: Source says 'with Judas,' not 'did with Judas'—Judas was with the Jews, not the one seized.
last_rejected.fix: as the Jews once did in the garden with Judas, when they seized the Lord (cf. John 18:3)
last_rejected.ruling: μετὰ Ἰούδα naturally means 'with Judas'; English 'did with Judas' captures the same scene without changing meaning.

last_rejected.why: ἀρνειός means 'lamb/ram,' but context requires 'lamb' to parallel Isaiah's prophecy (wolf/lamb, leopard/kid, lion/calf).
last_rejected.ruling: ἀρνειόν means 'lamb' or 'ram'; both fit normal range. Allusion is clear regardless of which English word is chosen.

last_rejected.quote: and after instructing him to tell no one what would be said
last_rejected.source_quote: μηδενί τε τὸ λεχθησόμενον ἐξειπεῖν παραγγείλαντες
last_rejected.why: μηδενί = 'to no one,' but the sense is 'after making him promise to tell no one what would be said'—'instructing' is too weak; they made him swear/promise secrecy.
last_rejected.fix: and after making him promise to tell no one what would be said
last_rejected.ruling: παραγγείλαντες means 'instructing/ordering'; 'instructing him to tell no one' accurately renders it. Preference for 'promise' is not error.

last_rejected.quote: to labor with them in the hunt for the man they sought
last_rejected.source_quote: συγκαμεῖν αὐτοῖς εἰς τὴν θήραν τοῦ ζητουμένου
last_rejected.why: συγκαμεῖν means 'to toil/work together with,' but in context they ask him to help in the hunt—'labor with' is awkward and slightly misses the collaborative sense of 'join in the toil.'
last_rejected.fix: to join them in the toil of hunting the man they sought
last_rejected.ruling: συγκαμεῖν = 'toil/work together'; 'labor with them in the hunt' correctly conveys collaborative effort. Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: he divided himself between two tasks
last_rejected.why: καταμερίζει means 'he divided/apportioned himself,' but 'tasks' is added—he divided himself between two things (welcoming murderers and preparing tomb). The addition of 'tasks' slightly changes sense.
last_rejected.fix: he divided himself between two things
last_rejected.ruling: καταμερίζει δυσὶ followed by two tasks; 'tasks' is implied ellipsis, not meaning change. Mere preference.
